BA: Green, blue and white horizontal stripes; shield bearing the silhouette of a fortified Bosnian town (mosque, churches) above the Vrbas, with a golden fleur-de-lys.
BC: Azure field on a green ground; the venerable patron of Bačka, robed in red, bearing the sword and the gospel.
BN: Red, blue and green horizontal tricolour; shield with the golden Nemanjić lion ascending fortified walls, beneath sun and crescent, the Danube and Tisa rivers, and the Serbian cross.
BR: Navy and white horizontal stripes; quartered shield, cross, mullet and anchor for the Danube heritage; on argent, the tower-on-bridge of historic Osijek; on gules, the otter of Baranja’s wetlands.
BS: Red, white and green horizontal tricolour; shield with the Ottoman crescent, the central Bosnian mountains and waters, and the golden Bosnian fleur-de-lys.
BZ: Yellow, blue and white horizontal tricolour; the crowned royal shield of the medieval Bosnian Kingdom, fleurs-de-lys and the silver bend, in heraldic descent from the Kotromanić dynasty.
CG: Crimson field with the golden double-headed eagle of the Nemanjić dynasty bearing the imperial monogram, historic ensign of the Petrović-Njegoš.
CM: Yellow field; on a red escutcheon, the rampant golden lion of Bulgarian heraldic continuity; black and azure stripes at the base recall the Black Sea littoral.
DA: Azure and or horizontal; on the chief, three crowned leopard heads, the historic arms of the Kingdom of Dalmatia, surmounted by the radiant sun of the Adriatic.
DJ: Sky-blue and maroon horizontal; a white seven-pointed mullet above; below, a sheaf of wheat, the grain wealth of southern Dobruja.
DR: Argent and gules horizontal; provincial shield with the chequy gules-argent of Croatia and the golden Ragusan lion on azure, surmounted by the mural crown of the Republic of Ragusa.
GV: Gules with two argent crosses, the Tirolean-Friulian heritage of the Goriška marches.
HZ: Navy field charged with the golden roundel of the Republic of Western Herzegovina, the Croatian chequy gules-argent within a laurel wreath, with the legend REPUBLIKA ZAPADNA HERCEGOVINA in capitals of gold.
HI: Per fess azure and vert; on a silver shield, the golden ibex of the Herzegovinian highlands, with horns banded gules; the sun radiant in chief.
IS: Or, gules and argent horizontal; central shield with the Veronese chequy and the golden Istrian lion on azure, Adriatic provincial heraldry.
KJ: Or field; on it, the red double-headed eagle, direct descent from the historic arms of the Duchy of Carinthia (Slovene Koroška).
KM: Serbian pan-colours, white-blue-red horizontal; on the central shield, the blue Habsburg-style eagle on argent with golden bend, heraldic continuity of Kosovska Mitrovica.
KR: Carmine, gold and azure horizontal tricolour, Carniolan and pan-Slovenian tradition, of solid stripe without charge.
KV: White, navy and white horizontal Adriatic stripes; on the central shield, the tower-on-bridge of the historic Gulf cities and the Kvarner pine marten at base.
LG: Vertical bands of vert, gules, argent, gules and vert; central shield of the Bulgarian Krum heritage, mural crown labelled “ЛUDOGOPIE” in Bulgarian Cyrillic, with the leaping Madara horseman.
LK: Azure field, charged in chief with the red Lika wolf rampant guardant, gripping an upright sword and surmounted by a coronet of liberty; argent and azure bars in base, totem of the highland uskoci.
MI: Per fess sable, argent and azure; on the argent band, the IYI rosette of Pliska, the imperial monogram of the First Bulgarian Empire, in sable on a circular cartouche.
MZ: Argent field; saltire of vert and gules interlaced; central shield argent with two lions rampant affrontés, surmounted by the sable kalpak of the Bulgarian voivodes, badged with a small or lion and pierced by a sword erect, heraldry of the haidouk liberation of the western Mizija.
PI: Gules field with the white crowned Serbian double-headed eagle bearing the Cross with four firesteels; in base, wavy bands of azure and argent, the Drina, root of the toponym Podriñe.
PM: Plain horizontal tricolour of celeste, gules and argent, pan-Slovenian banner of the trans-Mura territory, of solid stripe without charge.
PO: Vert field charged with a radiant sun in or, sixteen-pointed Vergina-style sun, the rising star over the Danubian plain.
PR: Red, vert and argent horizontal; central shield with the rocky peaks of Pirin, an Orthodox church of three domes between mountains, the golden bridge below, and the small Serbian cross-shield in base; scroll “ПОДРИЊЕ”.
PZ: Vert, gules and argent horizontal, Bulgarian-style stripe; from the hoist, a navy triangular pall charged with the Cyrillic letter Ш argent.
RO: Gules, azure and argent horizontal, Serbian pan-colours; central shield divided per bend, vert with three argent crescents (Ottoman heritage), azure with three golden fleurs-de-lys (Bosnian-style continuity for the Pomak community).
RS: Vert, azure and or horizontal; on the chief, the red Serbian cross with four firesteels; central shield with a stag couchant beneath a tree, between wavy bands of argent on azure, Sanxak in its highland forests.
SI: Azure, argent, gules, argent, azure, five horizontal stripes; on the gules band, the Srem marten running passant in proper colour; in chief, a golden eleven-pointed mullet on the azure of the heavens.
SL: Five horizontal stripes of or and gules alternating, pan-colours of the historic Kingdom of Slavonia, of solid stripe.
SP: Five horizontal stripes of gules and or alternating, pan-colours of the Šopski region.
ST: Argent and vert bipartite; on the central shield, the rampant Styrian panther in argent on a green field, the head crested with red flames; above, the imperial sun-crown, direct continuity of the historic arms of the Duchy of Styria.
SU: Serbian pan-colours, gules-azure-argent horizontal; on the central red shield, the sable boar’s head pierced by a sable arrow, the white Serbian cross with four firesteels at the base, totem of the Šumadija oak forests.
SX: Five horizontal stripes of gules and argent; from the hoist, a vert triangular pall charged with a golden radiant sun, Strandja highlands at the gates of Anatolia.
SZ: Five horizontal stripes of or and argent; on the central shield with wavy water in chief, a stag couchant beside an oak tree, all azure-argent-vert, heraldry of the Western Sirmian plain.
TK: Per fess gules, azure and or; on the azure middle band, a great twelve-pointed mullet of gold, the rising star of the Timok confluence.
TL: Pirot kilim borders top and base, guilloche of cream and indigo with rosettes; central red band bearing the Torlak fortress-and-cross shield, with scroll “ТОРЛАК” in Cyrillic.
TR: Quartered gules and azure with sable cross overall; central shield gules, the rampant Thracian lion or; above the cross, a small sun in gold, heraldic continuity of the historic Bulgarian Trakija.
VI: Gules field radiated by a yellow Vergina-style sun; over all, the golden crowned Macedonian lion rampant, heraldic continuity of the Kruševo Republic and the medieval Macedonian crown.
VZ: Gules, sable and gules horizontal, broad sable middle band; on the sable, the golden Byzantine double-headed eagle displayed, charged on its breast with the kolovrat sun-wheel and holding sceptre and orb, Byzantino-Slavic heritage of the Vardar marches.
